## 1 · Watch and pre-filter
Gmail Trigger runs only while the workflow is **Active**, and never backfills — it sees mail that arrives *after* activation.

The keyword/attachment filter is deliberately loose. It only exists to avoid spending an API call on every newsletter. Whether something really is an invoice is decided by Claude further down.

## 2 · Get the invoice text
PDF path: Extract From File (pdfjs) → quality gate.
No PDF: use the email body.

**The gate matters.** A corrupt file throws; a scanned page opens but yields no text. Either way Claude is never called, because handing a model an empty string invites a confident invented answer. OCR is out of scope, and that is recorded honestly.

## 3 · Extract with Claude
`tool_choice` pins the model to one tool, so the reply is always structured — no prose to parse.

The prompt forbids guessing: absent fields come back `null`. That is the point of the whole exercise — a blank cell is honest, an invented invoice number is not.

The HTTP node replaces `json`, so the email context is recovered by index from *Prepare For Claude*.

## Gate · invoice or not
Only records Claude confirms are invoices go on to be validated and logged - the sheet is a log of **invoices**, not of email traffic.

Rejected mail stops at *Not An Invoice - Skipped*, so it stays visible in the execution list without cluttering the sheet.

Corrupt files and API errors pass **through** this gate: those are failures to process, and the brief asks for them to be logged.

## 4 · Validate, then de-duplicate
Validation **flags**, it never repairs or blocks: anything missing or malformed is named in `error_note` and the row is still logged.

A Sheets read *replaces* the incoming items, so *Check Duplicate* takes the invoice from **Finalize Row** by name and the existing rows from its own input. Real rows carry `row_number`; the empty-sheet placeholder does not.

## 5 · Log the invoices
The sheet holds invoice records: `valid`, `valid_missing_fields`, plus the failures the brief asks to be recorded — `unsupported_attachment` and `extraction_failed` — each with an `error_note`.

Three things never produce a row: an email that was never a candidate, one Claude rules is not an invoice, and a duplicate. All three are visible in the execution list.
